facts.raw_span: A 14-year-old girl presented with a 6-year history of a photosensitive eruption involving her face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Her symptoms began at age 8 years

She had previously tried multiple medications including systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), with minimal improvement
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Diffuse poikiloderma involving upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
Nailfold examination showed dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)
Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies
Radiographic evidence of myositis
Confirmatory skin biopsy performed

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms, including photosensitive eruption, poikiloderma, and erythematous papules, along with elevated serum IFN-β levels and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, are consistent with Juvenile Dermatomyositis.
The patient's history of trying multiple medications with minimal improvement, along with the presence of autoantibodies and elevated serum IFN-β levels, suggests an underlying autoimmune disorder.
The patient's symptoms, including photosensitive eruption and poikiloderma, are consistent with a photosensitive eruption.
The patient's symptoms, including erythematous papules and radiographic evidence of myositis, are consistent with myositis.
The patient's symptoms, including diffuse poikiloderma, are consistent with poikiloderma.
The patient's presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, along with symptoms consistent with dermatomyositis, suggests anti-TIF-1γ autoantibody-associated dermatomyositis.
The patient's elevated serum IFN-β levels are consistent with an underlying autoimmune disorder.
The patient's confirmatory skin biopsy, along with symptoms consistent with dermatomyositis, suggests dermatomyositis with skin biopsy.

rationales.F01: Photosensitive eruption is a common symptom of dermatomyositis and photosensitive eruption.
rationales.F05: Poikiloderma is a characteristic skin finding in dermatomyositis.
rationales.F07: Nailfold capillary changes are a diagnostic feature of dermatomyositis.
rationales.F08: Elevated serum IFN-β levels are associated with anti-TIF-1γ autoantibody-associated dermatomyositis.
rationales.F09: Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies is a specific marker for anti-TIF-1γ autoantibody-associated dermatomyositis.
rationales.F10: Radiographic evidence of myositis supports the diagnosis of dermatomyositis and myositis.
rationales.F11: Confirmatory skin biopsy is a diagnostic feature of dermatomyositis with skin biopsy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's age, photosensitive eruption, and lack of response to multiple medications support Juvenile Dermatomyositis, while the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies and elevated serum IFN-β levels also suggest Anti-TIF-1γ Autoantibody-Associated Dermatomyositis, but the broader clinical presentation aligns more closely with Juvenile Dermatomyositis.
